u0: Starting point with no outstanding obligations: no client is waiting for an order, no food is held, and no dropped food needs retrieving. From here, client arrivals, pickups, and food slips will create commitments to take orders, fetch and prepare food, and serve it, and any slip must be picked up on the very next move.
u1: An order has been taken and nothing else is pending, so the client is now waiting to be served. The next required step is to fetch a portion of food from the pantry; slips are not currently a concern.
u10: A client has just arrived and their order has not been taken yet. The agent must go to the counter and take the order before any food work is needed.
u11: A client is present and an order has been taken, and the agent is carrying food. The food still needs preparing at the stove and then serving to the waiting client.
u12: A client has arrived, food is held, and the stove must be used while the client waits so the food becomes prepared. The prepared portion then has to be delivered to the counter.
u13: A client arrived as a portion slipped and was not recovered in time, so the one-step pickup rule is already broken. The new client's order must still be taken despite the slip failure.
u14: A slip was not recovered promptly but the portion is now held, and the newly arrived client's order still needs taking. The order, preparation, and serving chain lies ahead.
u15: A client arrived and a slip was mishandled, leaving both the order to take and the food workflow to complete. The one-step recovery requirement has already been broken.
u16: A freshly arrived client's order has been taken and nothing else is pending, so the agent must now fetch food from the pantry. The order itself was secured promptly.
u17: A new client is waiting, the order is taken, and prepared food is already available. It only remains to bring that food to the counter and serve the client.
u18: A client is waiting under a missed slip recovery, and food must still be fetched for their order. The one-step recovery rule has already been broken while the order workflow continues.
u19: An order was taken, food was prepared, but the slip recovery was mishandled; the prepared portion still needs to be served. The pending service and the failure of the one-step rule stand together.
u2: The agent is carrying food, so it must eventually prepare that food at the stove and then serve it to the waiting client. Retrieving dropped food in one move is not currently pending.
u20: The agent has taken the current client's order but is not yet carrying food; the order is secured, so the client-side requirement is met for now. It still needs to fetch food from the pantry and, once carried, prepare it at the stove and serve it to the waiting client. Food may slip on the way, in which case it must be picked up on the very next step.
u21: Here the agent has fallen food on the ground and has failed to pick it up on the very next step, so the immediate-pickup requirement is broken. It is carrying nothing but a client whose order is already taken is waiting. Completion is no longer possible; the machine is one step from the failure state.
u22: The agent is carrying food but no client order is currently outstanding, and the hands are full. Because food was carried, it is still committed to preparing that food at the stove and eventually serving it. It must keep hold of the portion (or recover it immediately if it slips) and finish the fetch-prepare-serve sequence.
u23: The agent is carrying food after having fallen and recovered it, with no order taken yet. It has already missed the one-step recovery deadline, so the food-slip requirement is broken even though the hands are full again. Further serving work is pointless for success.
u24: No order is taken and the hands are empty, but the client has already arrived. Taking that order is still owed and should be done without delay. After that, the agent must fetch food, prepare it, and serve the waiting client.
u25: The agent fell food and failed to pick it up on the next step, and it is not carrying any food now. No client order is outstanding. The immediate-recovery requirement has been violated, so the task can no longer be completed successfully.
u26: This is the failure state: a mandatory requirement has been violated and successful completion is no longer possible. The remaining work cannot restore the task's success conditions. Any further rewards are incidental.
u27: The agent has taken a client's order, holds no food, and food has not slipped. The order step is done, so it now owes fetching food and then preparing and serving it. It should head for the pantry before anything else interrupts the chain.
u28: Food slipped and stayed down for more than one step while a client's order was still taken. The recovery deadline was missed, so the task cannot be completed successfully. Continued play will not repair this.
u29: The agent has taken the current client's order and is not carrying food. The order requirement is satisfied, but it still owes fetching food from the pantry, preparing it at the stove, and serving it to the waiting client. If the food slips, it must pick it up immediately.
u3: Food has been prepared and served to the client at least once, returning the shop to a calm state with no pending obligations. New clients, pickups, or slips will each create fresh commitments.
u30: Food slipped and was left on the ground for more than one step, while an order had been taken. The one-step recovery rule is broken and success is impossible. The pending order and any later serving do not change that.
u31: The client has arrived and the agent has taken the order without yet picking up food. Fetching food, preparing it, and serving remain to be done. The next move in the sequence should be a trip to the pantry.
u32: Both the immediate-pickup rule and a later promise have been left unfulfilled after a slip with an order taken; the machine records several broken obligations. Completion is no longer achievable. The run can only continue for whatever side reward remains.
u4: An order was taken and food has already been prepared for it, so only serving the waiting client remains. The prepared food must be handed over at the counter.
u5: Food slipped out of the agent's hands and was not immediately picked up again, so the requirement to recover the food on the very next move has already been broken. Successful completion of that obligation is no longer possible, and the episode continues only with a penalty.
u6: A recovered slip left an order taken but no food yet fetched, so the agent must go to the pantry for a portion. The recovery itself already failed the one-step rule; the outstanding order still needs food and service.
u7: A slipped portion is still held in the hands and has been retrieved, but a waiting client's order requires preparation and serving. The outstanding order must still be completed with this food.
u8: A slip occurred, the food was not picked up on the immediately following step, and the food is now back in hand. Because the one-step recovery rule was missed, that obligation is failed even though other work continues.
u9: A slip was mishandled and an order is also outstanding on top of further pending obligations. The one-step recovery requirement has been broken, and the remaining food and serving tasks continue under that failure.
